newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Lenzing says trying to solve row with Courtaulds.
newsitem.headline: Lenzing says trying to solve row with Courtaulds.

text.p: Austrian fibres producer Lenzing AG confirmed on Thursday it was in discussions with Courtaulds Plc to try to solve its Lyocell patent dispute with the British chemicals group.

"Lenzing agree that it is clearly in both companies' interest to try to put patent disputes behind them and to concentrate their energies on developing this exciting new Lyocell market," said Leo Fermueller, member of Lenzing's board, in a statement.

Lenzing announced on Monday that the U.S. Federal Court of Appeal in Washington had confirmed its patent in the U.S., reversing the summary decision of the New York District Court in November 1995 which had ruled Lenzing's Lyocell patent invalid for failure to disclose the "best mode" of invention.
Lenzing had been claiming infringement of the patent by Courtaulds at its Lyocell plant in Mobile, Alabama, which Courtaulds denies on the assertion the patent was invalid.
Lenzing spokeswoman Rosemarie Schuller told Reuters the negotiations with Courtaulds were "taking place in a very good atmosphere and would continue." -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12256
